examples.ko: 창문을 열자 하얀 커튼이 천천히 너울거려요.
examples.en: When I open the window, the white curtain sways slowly.

examples.ko: 불꽃이 어둠 속에서 너울거리는 모습이 예뻐요.
examples.en: The flames waving in the dark look pretty.
A flag was waving over the sea.

examples.ko: 긴 치마가 걸을 때마다 너울거려서 시원해 보여요.
examples.en: The long skirt flutters with every step, so it looks cool.

examples.ko: 해초가 물속에서 너울거릴 때마다 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo every time the seaweed swayed in the water.
The dancer's sleeves flow as the dance goes on.

explain: '펄럭이다'가 바람에 세게 흔들리는 느낌이라면 '너울거리다'는 천, 불꽃, 해초가 부드럽고 느리게 크게 흔들리는 모습이에요. 주로 글이나 묘사에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '살랑거리다'나 '흔들리다'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: While '펄럭이다' feels like something flapping hard in the wind, '너울거리다' describes cloth, flames or seaweed swaying softly, slowly and widely. It is mostly used in writing and description; in speech people also say '살랑거리다' or '흔들리다'.

examples.en: A butterfly flutters around over the flower bed.
The curtain moves softly in the wind.

examples.ko: 무용수가 소매를 너울너울 흔들며 춤을 춰요.
examples.en: The dancer waves her sleeves gracefully as she dances.
The seaweed sways gently in the water.
The smoke rises into the sky in lazy waves.
The flag looks like it is dancing slowly.

explain: '펄럭펄럭'이 빠르고 센 움직임이라면 '너울너울'은 느긋하고 부드럽게 크게 흔들리는 모양이에요. 뒤에 '날다, 흔들리다, 움직이다' 같은 동사와 함께 써요.
explain_en: '펄럭펄럭' is a fast, strong flapping, but '너울너울' is a relaxed, soft and wide swaying. It is used before verbs such as '날다', '흔들리다' and '움직이다'.

examples.ko: 태풍이 지나간 뒤 바다가 크게 너울졌어요.
examples.en: After the typhoon passed, the sea rolled with big swells.

examples.ko: 너울지는 파도 때문에 배가 많이 흔들려요.
examples.en: The boat rocks a lot because of the rolling swells.
The sea was swelling, so I couldn't fish.
Waves from far away come in as long swells.
They say the sea may swell today.
The clouds drift over the mountain in rolling waves.

explain: 바람이 불지 않아도 먼 바다의 영향으로 크고 길게 일렁이는 물결을 말할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '너울성 파도'라는 말로도 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes big, long, rolling water that can appear even without wind, caused by conditions far out at sea. You may also hear it in the news as '너울성 파도' (swell waves).

examples.ko: 방이 너무 너절해서 손님을 못 불러요.
examples.en: My room is so shabby that I can't invite guests.

examples.ko: 너절한 옷차림으로 면접에 가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't go to an interview in shabby clothes.

examples.ko: 책상 위가 너절해 보이니까 좀 치우세요.
examples.en: Your desk looks messy, so please tidy it up.
Stop making cheap excuses.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 겉은 멀쩡한데 안은 너절해요.
examples.en: That shop looks fine outside but is shabby inside.
It is a storage room full of nothing but junk.

explain: '지저분하다'가 더러운 느낌이라면 '너절하다'는 허름하고 질이 낮아 보이는 느낌이 강해요. 물건이나 옷차림뿐 아니라 말이나 행동이 치사할 때도 써요. 비슷한 '너저분하다'는 물건이 어지럽게 널린 모습에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: '지저분하다' means dirty or messy, while '너절하다' stresses a cheap, low-quality look. It can describe things and clothes, and also petty words or behavior. The similar '너저분하다' is closer to things lying around in disorder.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 내 이야기를 듣고 너털웃음을 터뜨리셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather burst into a hearty laugh when he heard my story.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 일도 없었다는 듯 너털웃음을 지었어요.
examples.en: He gave a hearty laugh as if nothing had happened.
The boss's booming laughter could be heard down the hallway.
My father eased the mood with a big, easy laugh.
When his mistake was pointed out, he just laughed it off heartily.
My friend patted my shoulder with a hearty laugh.

explain: 크고 시원하게, 걱정 없이 웃는 웃음이에요. '너털웃음을 웃다/짓다/터뜨리다'처럼 써요. 어이가 없어서 나오는 '헛웃음'과는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a big, open, carefree laugh, used as '너털웃음을 웃다/짓다/터뜨리다'. It feels different from '헛웃음', the empty laugh that comes out of disbelief.

examples.en: The laundry hung on the roof flutters in the wind.
His hair fluttered every time he ran.
I took photos in a flowing skirt.
The big shirt flaps around, so it's a bit uncomfortable.
The Korean flag is waving in front of the school.

examples.ko: 너풀거릴 정도로 큰 옷은 사지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't buy clothes so big that they flap around.

explain: 천이나 머리카락처럼 얇고 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 흔들릴 때 써요. 헐렁한 옷이 몸 주위에서 흔들리는 모습에도 잘 어울려요. '너울거리다'는 더 느리고 크게 물결치는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when something thin and light, like cloth or hair, keeps moving in the wind. It also fits loose clothes flapping around the body. '너울거리다' feels slower and more wavelike.

examples.en: The skirt flutters in the wind.
A butterfly fluttered over and landed on my shoulder.
The loose shirt flaps back and forth.
The child runs off with a scarf fluttering behind.
The towels dance on the clothesline.
The hem of the coat fluttered.

explain: 얇은 천이나 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 흔들리는 모양이에요. 뒤에 '날리다, 흔들리다, 움직이다' 같은 동사가 잘 와요.
explain_en: It describes thin cloth or light things moving back and forth in the wind. Verbs like '날리다', '흔들리다' and '움직이다' often follow it.

en: allow enough time; set enough amount

examples.en: Allowing plenty of time, you'll get to the airport in an hour.
Even at the most generous estimate, the homework takes two days.
I'll prepare enough for ten people, to be safe.
I bought twenty breads to be on the safe side.
The cost is about one million won at the high end.
The more leeway you allow for the moving date, the more relaxed you feel.

explain: 주로 '넉넉잡아', '넉넉잡아도' 꼴로 써서 시간, 양, 비용을 여유 있게 어림할 때 말해요. '넉넉하게 잡다'라고 풀어 말해도 같아요. 반대로 빠듯하게 계산할 때는 '빠듯하게 잡다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '넉넉잡아' or '넉넉잡아도' when estimating time, amount or cost with room to spare. Saying '넉넉하게 잡다' means the same. The opposite idea is '빠듯하게 잡다' (to estimate tightly).

examples.ko: 그 친구는 넉살이 좋아서 어디서나 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: That friend is so easygoing and cheeky that he fits in anywhere.

examples.ko: 넉살 좋은 동생 덕분에 분위기가 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my brazen but charming younger brother, the mood relaxed.

examples.ko: 그는 넉살을 부리며 음료수를 공짜로 얻었어요.
examples.en: He charmed his way into getting a free drink.

examples.ko: 처음 보는 사람한테도 넉살 좋게 말을 걸어요.
examples.en: He cheerfully talks even to people he's just met.
You've got some nerve even in front of the department head.
He got through the awkward situation with his cheeky charm.

explain: '넉살이 좋다'라는 말로 가장 많이 써요. 부끄러워하지 않고 능청스럽게 구는 성격인데, '뻔뻔하다'보다 밉지 않고 친근한 느낌일 때가 많아요. 상황에 따라 칭찬일 수도, 약간의 흉일 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is most often used in '넉살이 좋다'. It means being shameless and playfully bold, usually in a friendlier way than '뻔뻔하다'. Depending on the situation it can be a compliment or a light criticism.

examples.en: He sat down with a cheeky smile.

examples.ko: 넉살스러운 말투 때문에 미워할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I can't dislike him because of his cheeky way of talking.

examples.ko: 동생이 넉살스러워서 처음 만난 사람과도 금방 친해져요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is so bold and friendly that he gets close to new people fast.

examples.ko: 넉살스럽다고 해서 예의가 없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being cheeky doesn't mean being rude.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 넉살스러워서 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The new employee is so outgoing that the atmosphere got better.
He asked for pocket money with a cheeky look.

explain: 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '넉살스러워요'로 바뀌어요. 부끄러움 없이 능청스럽게 구는 모습인데, '넉살이 좋다'와 비슷하게 밉지 않고 친근한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '넉살스러워요'. It describes a person acting boldly and playfully without embarrassment, usually in a likable, friendly way, similar to '넉살이 좋다'.

examples.ko: 친구의 넋두리를 두 시간이나 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: I listened to my friend's grumbling for two whole hours.

examples.ko: 그는 신세 한탄 같은 넋두리를 계속 늘어놓아요.
examples.en: He keeps going on with self-pitying complaints.

examples.ko: 힘든 일이 있으면 저한테 넋두리라도 하세요.
examples.en: If something is hard, at least vent to me.
Grandmother's lament went on so long that the meal got cold.
This isn't a complaint, just me venting.

examples.ko: 넋두리만 하지 말고 해결 방법을 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's look for a solution instead of just grumbling.

explain: 보통 '넋두리를 하다/늘어놓다'로 써요. 신세나 억울한 일을 혼잣말처럼 길게 투덜대는 느낌이고, '푸념'과 비슷해요. 해결을 바라기보다 속상한 마음을 쏟아내는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '넋두리를 하다/늘어놓다'. It feels like long, mumbling grumbling about your lot or something unfair, similar to '푸념'. It is about pouring out frustration rather than seeking a solution.

examples.en: My friend grumbled to me on the phone for a long time.
It's okay to vent once in a while when things are hard.
My father keeps complaining that his pay is low.

examples.ko: 넋두리할 사람이 없어서 혼자 일기를 써요.
examples.en: I have no one to vent to, so I write in a diary.
Grumbling won't change anything.
Stop grumbling and let's find a way together.

explain: '넋두리를 하다'를 줄여 한 단어로 쓴 말이에요. 불평을 길게 늘어놓는 모습이라 '넋두리하지 말고'처럼 핀잔을 줄 때도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It packs '넋두리를 하다' into one verb. Because it pictures long, drawn-out complaining, it often appears in mild scolding like '넋두리하지 말고'.

en: having enough of something; being weary

examples.en: I'm sick and tired of working overtime every day.

examples.ko: 그 이야기는 이제 넌더리가 날 만큼 들었어요.
examples.en: I've heard that story so often that I'm fed up with it.

examples.ko: 같은 반찬이 계속 나와서 넌더리가 났어요.
examples.en: The same side dish kept coming out, and I got sick of it.
He is fed up with people who lie.

examples.ko: 장마철 습기에 넌더리를 느끼는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people are fed up with the humidity of the rainy season.

examples.ko: 이 일에는 정말 넌더리가 나서 그만두고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm so sick of this job that I want to quit.

explain: 거의 '넌더리가 나다', '넌더리를 내다' 꼴로 써요. 같은 일이 계속되어 진저리가 날 때 쓰는데, '지겹다'나 '질리다'보다 싫은 마음이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '넌더리가 나다' or '넌더리를 내다'. It is for being fed up with something that keeps happening, and the dislike is stronger than in '지겹다' or '질리다'.

examples.en: On Lunar New Year, I played neolttwigi with my sister in hanbok.
Kite flying, jegi kicking and neolttwigi are Korean folk games.
At the folk village, I watched children playing neolttwigi.
In the old days, women played neolttwigi in the first lunar month.
The stock price swings up and down wildly, so I'm anxious.

examples.ko: 한 번도 널뛰어 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I've never tried neolttwigi even once.

explain: 긴 널빤지 양쪽에 한 사람씩 올라서서 번갈아 뛰는 전통 놀이예요. 보통 '널뛰기'라는 명사로 말하고 '널뛰기를 하다'도 써요. 가격이나 기분이 크게 오르내릴 때 '널뛰듯'이라고 비유해서도 말해요.

phrases.en: My emotions have been all over the place lately, and it's hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분이나 가격이 안정되지 않고 크게 오르내릴 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for moods or prices that swing wildly without settling.

explain_en: It is a traditional game where one person stands on each end of a long board and they jump in turn. People usually say the noun '널뛰기', as in '널뛰기를 하다'. It is also used figuratively as '널뛰듯' when prices or moods swing up and down.

examples.en: The puppy gobbled up the treat in a flash.

examples.ko: 동생이 내 케이크를 널름 집어 먹었어요.
examples.en: My brother snatched up my cake and ate it.
The frog snaps up a bug with its tongue.
The child gave the ice cream a quick lick.

examples.ko: 그는 돈을 널름 받아 주머니에 넣었어요.
examples.en: He took the money quickly and put it in his pocket.

examples.ko: 눈 깜짝할 새에 반찬이 널름 사라졌어요.
examples.en: The side dishes vanished in the blink of an eye.

explain: 혀를 재빨리 내밀거나 무언가를 날쌔게 받아먹고 집어 가는 모양이에요. 작은말 '날름'이 더 가볍고 작은 느낌이에요. 가끔 약삭빠르게 챙기는 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes quickly sticking out the tongue, or swiftly taking and eating something. The smaller-sounding '날름' feels lighter and smaller. It can also carry a sense of quickly helping oneself.

examples.en: The snake came closer, flicking its tongue.

examples.ko: 난로 불길이 널름거리는 걸 한참 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the flames licking in the stove for a while.
The puppy waits for a treat, licking its lips.
The lizard flicked its tongue in and out, which was fascinating.
Flames began to lick up over the roof.
The baby sticking its tongue in and out is cute.

explain: 혀나 불길이 빠르게 나왔다 들어갔다 하는 모습에 써요. 작은말은 '날름거리다'예요. 물결이 크게 흔들리는 '너울거리다'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It describes a tongue or flames quickly darting out and back in. The smaller-sounding version is '날름거리다'. Don't confuse it with '너울거리다', which is about large, soft waving.

examples.en: Clothes are scattered all over the floor.
I was tired, so I flopped onto the sofa and fell asleep.
After the exam, my friends slumped around the classroom.
Documents were strewn on the desk, so I tidied them up.

examples.ko: 더운 날씨에 강아지가 바닥에 널브러져 있어요.
examples.en: In the hot weather, the dog is sprawled out on the floor.

examples.ko: 널브러진 짐을 치우느라 한 시간 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took an hour to clear away the scattered bags.

explain: 물건이 아무렇게나 흩어져 있을 때도, 사람이 힘없이 축 늘어져 있을 때도 써요. '흩어지다'는 여기저기 퍼지는 느낌이고, '널브러지다'는 어지럽게 놓이거나 늘어진 모습이에요. 보통 '널브러져 있다' 꼴로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used both for things lying scattered at random and for a person sprawled out limply. '흩어지다' feels like spreading in different directions, while '널브러지다' is about a messy, slumped state. It often appears as '널브러져 있다'.

examples.ko: 기부한 사람들의 이름을 금액 순서대로 널판에 써 붙였어요.
examples.en: They wrote the donors' names on a board in order of amount.
My father cut a board and made a shelf.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 널판 위로 걸어서 건넜어요.
examples.en: It had rained, so we crossed by walking over a board.

examples.ko: 창고 문에 널판을 대서 구멍을 막았어요.
examples.en: I put a board over the hole in the warehouse door.

examples.ko: 공사장 입구에 널판이 길게 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Long boards are laid at the entrance to the construction site.

examples.ko: 이 널판은 두껍고 단단해서 책상으로 쓰기 좋아요.
examples.en: This board is thick and sturdy, so it works well as a desk.

explain: 넓고 얇게 켠 나무 조각을 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '널빤지'도 있는데, 일상 대화에서는 '널빤지'를 더 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '판자'도 있어요.
explain_en: It means a wide, thin cut piece of wood. '널빤지' means the same and is more common in everyday talk. '판자' is a similar word.

examples.en: Don't just assume what I'm thinking.

examples.ko: 이유도 모르면서 넘겨짚어서 말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't speak by guessing when you don't know the reason.
He jumped to the conclusion that I was angry.
I made a mistake by assuming without checking.

examples.ko: 사람을 외모로 넘겨짚는 건 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not good to judge people by appearance.
I was surprised that my guess turned out to be right.

explain: 근거가 부족한데도 미리 짐작해서 말하거나 판단하는 거예요. '추측하다'는 중립적이지만 '넘겨짚다'는 틀릴 수 있다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '넘겨짚지 마세요'처럼 상대에게 조심하라고 할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means guessing or judging ahead of time without enough basis. '추측하다' is neutral, but '넘겨짚다' carries a negative feeling that you might be wrong. It is often used in warnings like '넘겨짚지 마세요'.

examples.en: I gazed at the sea, its waves rolling.

examples.ko: 강물이 비 때문에 둑 위까지 넘실거려요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the river water surges up to the bank.
The golden barley field ripples in the wind.
The water in the glass was nearly spilling, so I carried it carefully.
I like the sound of waves rolling in.
Joy welled up in my heart.

explain: 큰 물결이 부드럽게 크게 일렁이는 모습이에요. '출렁이다'가 흔들리는 것 자체를 말한다면 '넘실거리다'는 물이 넘칠 듯 가득한 느낌이 있어요. 감정이 가득 차오를 때 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes large waves rising and falling softly and widely. While '출렁이다' is about the shaking itself, '넘실거리다' has a brimming, almost overflowing feel. It is also used figuratively when emotions swell up.

examples.en: The waves roll in, swelling and falling.
The river flows with big, soft swells.
The barley field ripples in the wind.

examples.ko: 물이 넘실넘실 찬 컵을 조심히 옮겼어요.
examples.en: I carefully carried the cup, brimming with water.
A big ship drifts on the rolling sea.
In the autumn fields, the rice waves in great ripples.

explain: 물결이나 곡식이 크고 부드럽게 일렁이는 모양이에요. 뒤에 '흐르다, 흔들리다, 물결치다' 같은 동사가 잘 와요. '출렁출렁'보다 물이 가득 차서 크게 움직이는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes water or crops moving in big, soft swells. Verbs like '흐르다', '흔들리다' and '물결치다' often follow. Compared with '출렁출렁', it feels fuller, as if the water is brimming.

examples.en: There's a child peeking over the wall.
Don't peer over into the neighbor's yard.

examples.ko: 그는 울타리 너머로 집 안을 넘어다봤어요.
examples.en: He looked over the fence into the house.

examples.ko: 키가 작아서 벽을 넘어다볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: I'm short, so I can't see over the wall.
The child waits for Mom, peeking over the fence.
It's rude to peek over at someone else's desk.

explain: 담이나 벽처럼 사이에 있는 것 너머로 건너편을 몰래 또는 슬쩍 보는 거예요. '넘겨다보다'도 비슷하게 써요. 남의 것을 엿볼 때 쓰는 경우가 많아서 조금 실례되는 느낌이 있을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means looking at the other side over something in between, such as a wall, often stealthily or quickly. '넘겨다보다' is used in a similar way. It is often about peeking at other people's things, so it can sound slightly rude.

examples.en: The child bowed deeply to the adults.
I dropped down to bow for the New Year greeting.
When given pocket money, my brother took it without a second thought.
When I asked, he answered right away.
I readily accepted and ate the snack the teacher offered.
He accepted the request without hesitating.

explain: '넙죽 엎드리다', '넙죽 절하다'처럼 몸을 바닥에 크게 숙일 때 써요. 또 주는 것이나 부탁을 망설임 없이 덥석 받을 때도 써요. 상황에 따라 시원시원하다는 느낌도, 염치없다는 느낌도 줄 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '넙죽 엎드리다' or '넙죽 절하다' when bowing low to the floor. It also describes accepting a gift or request without hesitation. Depending on the situation it can sound straightforward or a bit shameless.

examples.ko: 오래 입은 옷이 넝마가 되어 버렸어요.
examples.en: The clothes I wore for so long turned into rags.

examples.ko: 그는 넝마 같은 옷을 입고 서 있었어요.
examples.en: He stood there wearing clothes that looked like rags.

examples.ko: 헌 티셔츠를 넝마로 모아서 걸레로 써요.
examples.en: I collect old T-shirts as rags and use them for cleaning.

examples.ko: 이 담요는 너무 낡아서 넝마나 다름없어요.
examples.en: This blanket is so worn it is no better than a rag.
After wearing them a few days, the pants looked like rags.

examples.ko: 넝마를 이어 붙여 만든 가방이 인기예요.
examples.en: Bags made by stitching together scraps of old cloth are popular.

explain: 낡고 해진 천이나 헌 옷을 말해요. 비슷한 '누더기'는 여기저기 기운 낡은 옷의 느낌이 강하고, '넝마'는 헌 천이나 헌 옷감 자체를 가리키는 느낌이에요. '넝마가 되다'처럼 심하게 해지거나 망가진 상태를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It means worn-out, tattered cloth or old clothes. The similar '누더기' leans toward a patched, ragged garment, while '넝마' points to the old cloth itself. It also appears in '넝마가 되다' for something badly worn out or ruined.
